entry.note: Stay length unresolved (checked 2026-11-01): the 30-day route text came from the former embassy FAQ (now a 404). Emirates airline lists Australians for a free 90-day multiple-entry visa on arrival; the UAE Ministry of Economy and Tourism says on-arrival stays are 30 or 90 days by nationality but gives no list. Confirm with ICP or GDRFA.

tourism.detail: The UAE Embassy in Canberra states that eligible Australian passport holders receive the visitor visa at the airport or another entry point.
tourism.next: Travel with six months' passport validity, onward travel and accommodation evidence, then check the authorised last day on arrival.
tourism.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

meetings.route: 30-day visitor entry for discussion and market scouting
meetings.detail: Use the visitor stay for partner, publisher, university, venue, supplier and investor meetings without delivering the contracted service.
meetings.next: Keep the invitation meeting-only; if a workshop, installation or advisory session is added, have the host reclassify it before delivery.
meetings.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

conference.detail: Attendance and networking can use the visitor lane. Exhibiting, demonstrating, selling, speaking or staffing a stand can add work, customs, event and media questions.
conference.next: Ask the organiser to state delegate versus active exhibitor or program role and list any equipment or stock entering the UAE.
conference.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

unpaid-speaking.route: Host classification; Mission Work Permit where the appearance is treated as short project work
unpaid-speaking.detail: No fee does not by itself make a keynote, panel, reading or facilitated session tourism. Media regulation can apply to media activities whether paid or unpaid, and emirate event permissions can also matter.
unpaid-speaking.next: Have the host obtain written classification from its labour, venue and media channels before advertising the appearance.
unpaid-speaking.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

paid-speaking.route: Mission Work Permit through a licensed UAE establishment
paid-speaking.detail: The permit is designed for short-term project employment, runs for three months and can be renewed once. The UAE payer must also classify tax, invoicing and any emirate-level event approval.
paid-speaking.next: Contract through the UAE host, obtain the official job offer and permit before delivery, and have the payer confirm corporate-tax and withholding treatment in writing.
paid-speaking.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

book-launch.route: Mission Work Permit or other work route plus publisher, venue and media approvals
book-launch.detail: Rights meetings can stay in the visitor lane. A public talk, signing, paid promotion or sale is active delivery. Publications imported for circulation require a UAE Media Council permit, and local publisher or bookseller handling is the cleanest first model.
book-launch.next: Split rights meetings, author appearance, book import, retail and online promotion, then assign each part to a UAE publisher, bookseller, venue or licensed agency.
book-launch.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

ai-teaching.route: Mission Work Permit plus education approval where the role is regulated
ai-teaching.detail: A short company or conference workshop can fit the project permit. MOHRE lists teachers among professions for which a competent-authority licence can be required; university, school and public training contexts should be classified by the host.
ai-teaching.next: Get a host letter specifying guest lecture, public workshop, staff training or formal teaching, and obtain any education-authority approval before travel.
ai-teaching.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

remote-work.route: Virtual Work Residence for employment outside the UAE
remote-work.detail: The ICP service requires proof of remote employment outside the UAE, a passport valid for six months and a salary certificate showing at least USD 3,500 or equivalent. It is a purpose-built route rather than a visitor-work assumption.
remote-work.next: Apply through ICP with the overseas employment and salary evidence; keep UAE clients and local delivery outside this lane.
remote-work.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

entrepreneur.route: Licensed business plus Green or Golden Residence where eligible
entrepreneur.detail: Green Residence is a renewable five-year sponsor-free route for qualifying investors, partners and self-employed people. Freelancers need a permit, qualification and at least AED 360,000 annual freelance income in each of the previous two years. Golden Residence has separate entrepreneur, investor and exceptional-talent evidence.
entrepreneur.next: Choose emirate and mainland or free-zone activity first, obtain the exact licence, then test Green or Golden Residence rather than assuming company ownership gives work rights.
entrepreneur.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

trade.route: Visitor meetings; Mission Work Permit and licensed entity for delivery
trade.detail: Negotiations, sourcing and partner discovery can stay in the meeting lane. Demonstration, installation, local retail, fulfilment or service delivery can become work and licensed trade. Temporary equipment and sale stock need customs planning.
trade.next: Use a UAE importer, distributor or event contractor for the first active trade trip and itemise samples, professional gear and goods for sale.
trade.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

artist.route: Mission Work Permit plus promoter, venue and media approvals
artist.detail: Music, film, visual art, literary and cultural appearances need host-led work classification whether paid or unpaid. Golden Residence may support qualifying accredited creative talent for a longer base, but it is not an instant event permit.
artist.next: Have the promoter confirm the work permit, venue or event approval, content review, tax and merchandise arrangements before public announcement.
artist.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

mixed-mission.route: Visitor entry plus Mission Work Permit or residence and activity-specific approvals
mixed-mission.detail: A single trip can combine meetings, speaking, AI training, books, art and remote work, but the visitor visa does not absorb every activity. Each emirate and free zone can add a different licensing layer.
mixed-mission.next: Build one activity ledger by emirate, venue, host, payer, audience, stock and media use; obtain a written route decision for every active line.
mixed-mission.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

filming.route: Advance permission from the UAE Media Regulatory Office
filming.detail: Smartraveller: media activity (producing, transmitting or distributing printed, digital, audio, video or visual information) needs permission in advance; without it you can be arrested and deported.
filming.next: Register with the Media Regulatory Office before travel.

volunteering.detail: Smartraveller: make sure charity or volunteer organisations are registered with the UAE Government before you take part.

research.route: Events Visit Visa covers conferences and educational activities, not research
research.detail: The Events Visit Visa covers conferences, seminars and educational activities on the host's invitation. Fieldwork or research is not named.
research.next: Ask the host institution in writing.

laws.rule: If you come to the attention of UAE authorities, your case will be dealt with by the local legal and judicial system. This differs significantly from Australia's legal system. If you're arrested, authorities may hold you for an unspecified length of time before your case goes to trial. UAE authorities can hold your passport and stop you from leaving the country. Even simple legal issues can take a long time to resolve. Custodial sentences are served in local jails. If you're going to be deported, you'll be in immigration detention for at least 24 hours before being allowed to leave the UAE. To get a list of lawyers who can represent you, either: download from Consular Assistance call the Con
laws.heading: Legal process

laws.rule: The UAE is made up of 7 emirates, each with its own justice system. Laws, legal procedures and penalties vary between systems. There's a federal court system with a final court of appeal in Abu Dhabi. This is called the Federal Supreme Court. Dubai and Ras Al Khaimah aren't part of this system.
laws.heading: Laws in individual emirates

laws.rule: Australians are often involved in disputes where local firms or courts have taken their passport. This prevents them from leaving the UAE until the dispute is settled. You can be jailed or stopped from leaving the UAE for offences including: having a cheque dishonoured not paying bills, including court fines, hotel bills, personal loans and local credit cards Immigration authorities can refuse you entry if you have a criminal record. It won't matter how long ago the offence took place. If you travel to the UAE with an active case against you, including an unpaid UAE debt, authorities are likely to detain you on arrival. This applies even if you're only in transit and don't plan to leave the
laws.heading: Commercial, civil and family law disputes

laws.rule: The UAE has a zero-tolerance policy towards drugs, including for travellers transiting through the country. Penalties for drug trafficking may include the death penalty, or a sentence up to life imprisonment. Penalties for having or using illegal drugs include lengthy jail terms and heavy fines. These laws also apply if you're transiting through the UAE. If illegal drugs are found in blood or urine tests, this is considered possession. It won't matter where or how long ago you consumed the drugs. You can be charged with possession if trace amounts of drugs are found on your body, clothing or luggage. You can be convicted for 0.05g or less. Avoid carrying substances that could be mistaken for
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: You must obtain permission in advance from the Emirati authorities to undertake media activity relating to the production, transmission or distribution of printed, digital, audio, video or visual information. If you fail to do this, you could be arrested and deported from the UAE. You can get more information on obtaining the necessary permits to carry out media activity in the UAE and bringing media equipment into the UAE by registering online at the Media Regulatory Office website.
laws.heading: Media activity

laws.rule: You can be fined, jailed or deported for: insulting other people, the UAE, the royal families, the local government or local officials disrespecting the UAE flag discriminating against or insulting a racial, ethnic or religious group making rude gestures making inappropriate or offensive comments on social media swearing touching another person without their permission taking photos or videos of military conflict, airports and transport infrastructure, bridges, government buildings, embassies and palaces. publishing, sharing or reposting rumours or unverified information online. It's illegal to harass women in the UAE. Behaviour that may offend or be considered illegal includes: glaring ogli
laws.heading: Criminal acts

laws.rule: You can be arrested for intimate public displays of affection, including kissing. This behaviour can attract the attention of local authorities. See Local customs below.
laws.heading: Public displays of affection

laws.rule: If you engage in unauthorised preaching or distribute non-Islamic religious material to Muslims, you can be jailed and deported. If you make offensive comments about Islam either in writing or verbally, you could be jailed or subject to other penalties.
laws.heading: Unauthorised preaching

laws.rule: The UAE has strict laws about online behaviour, including comments. Online behaviour that may be considered a crime includes: spreading rumours or gossip defamation of an individual or business swearing and insulting others extortion and making threats or accusations posting photos of local incidents, such as building fires or storm damage using a fake IP address, such as a Virtual Private Network (VPN), to commit or cover up a crime Punishments for these crimes include: fines jail terms deportation Charity and fundraising activities are closely regulated, including when conducted online and via social media. Make sure charity or volunteer organisations are registered with the UAE Government
laws.heading: Social media and behaviour online

laws.rule: Heterosexual sex and cohabitation outside of marriage for individuals over 18 years old have been decriminalised in all Emirates except for Sharjah. Extra-marital sexual relationships (adultery) is illegal in the UAE. If either person's spouse or parent/guardian files a criminal complaint, then both parties of an extra-marital consensual relationship shall be liable to a jail sentence.
laws.heading: Sex outside of marriage

laws.rule: Same-sex relationships are illegal and may lead to severe punishment, including prison and fines. Cross-dressing is also illegal. If you're transgender or intersex, or your gender on your passport doesn't match your appearance, you may: be questioned at immigration be denied entry into the UAE If you're travelling on an Australian passport showing 'X' or 'U' (indeterminate, intersex or unspecified) in the gender field, you won't be able to enter or transit the UAE.
laws.heading: LGBTQIA+ information

laws.rule: Prostitution is illegal in the UAE. Severe penalties apply to: people providing prostitution services customers of prostitution services
laws.heading: Prostitution

laws.rule: If you're unmarried and fall pregnant or give birth in the UAE and wish to obtain a local birth certificate, both you and your partner will need to either get married or you and/or your partner must singly or jointly acknowledge the child and provide documentation in accordance with the laws of your country.
laws.heading: Registering births of children born to unmarried parents

laws.rule: Although a Federal law has decriminalised the use of alcohol, every Emirate has its own guidelines. The Emirate of Sharjah is 'dry' which means the sale or consumption of alcohol is illegal. You can't carry alcohol in your car if you're: driving through Sharjah crossing the border from Oman into Sharjah There are limits on how much duty-free alcohol you can bring in. These limits are strictly enforced.
laws.heading: Alcohol

laws.rule: Liquor licences are still required for residents in Dubai but are no longer required for residents in Abu Dhabi and other Emirates (except for Sharjah) to purchase alcohol for personal consumption. A liquor licence is only valid in the Emirate that issues it. For example, a liquor licence issued in Ras Al Khaimah isn't valid in Dubai.
laws.heading: Liquor licences

laws.rule: The legal drinking age in Abu Dhabi is 18 years. However, the Ministry of Tourism by-law means hotels can only serve alcohol to people aged over 21 years. The legal drinking age in Dubai and the northern Emirates, except for Sharjah, is 21 years.
laws.heading: Legal drinking age

laws.rule: It's illegal to be intoxicated in public outside of licenced venues. You can be arrested. Authorities have arrested travellers at the airport for becoming intoxicated on a flight or while in transit. Be careful if you're using a taxi when intoxicated. If you have a dispute with a driver or vomit in a taxi, you may be: taken directly to a police station charged with public intoxication If you commit a crime after drinking alcohol, you'll probably be charged with both that offence and with intoxication. Penalties for alcohol-related offences include fines, jail or deportation.
laws.heading: Drinking in public

laws.rule: You must have a valid work permit from the UAE Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation for any type of employment. If you plan to work, sort out terms and conditions or sponsorship before starting. This will minimise the risk of a dispute. If you get into a dispute, a special department of the UAE Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation can review and help settle your claim. Your UAE employer may ask to hold your passport as a condition of employment. This is illegal, but not unusual. An employer can hold your passport for a short time when arranging, renewing or cancelling your visa or work permit. If your passport is held for a longer period, either: make a complaint to the UAE
laws.heading: Employment

laws.rule: Serious crimes can attract the death penalty. Serious crimes include: murder spying terrorism treason rape The UAE Government has a list of groups it considers to be terrorist organisations. If you're associated with such groups, you could be refused entry or arrested and detained. In the UAE it's illegal to: carry weapons, including pocketknives and capsicum or pepper spray discriminate through speech, written word or online media vandalise religious symbols, rituals or holy rites Penalties for discriminating and vandalising can include: jail terms of 6 months to more than 10 years fines of up to AED2 million
laws.heading: Other legal issues

laws.rule: You must have written approval from the UAE Ministry of Defence to transport law enforcement or military equipment into or through the UAE. This equipment includes: ammunition body armour handcuffs military equipment police equipment weapons weapon parts and tools Australians, including those transiting through UAE airports, have been punished for transporting this equipment without written approval. Some have been jailed or deported.
laws.heading: Law enforcement and military equipment

laws.rule: It's illegal to photograph: people without permission airports and related transport infrastructure bridges government buildings, including embassies palaces Taking part in some hobbies, particularly around these sites, can break the law.
laws.heading: Photography and other hobbies

laws.rule: It's illegal for residents to drive without a UAE driver's licence once they have residency. Non-residents and travellers must have an International Driving Permit (IDP). Although common in the UAE, it's illegal to use a mobile phone, eat or drink while driving. Other illegal activities include: jaywalking walking on highways hitchhiking It's illegal to drive after drinking alcohol. You may be jailed or fined if you have any alcohol in your blood when driving. These laws are strictly enforced in the UAE. Police must be called to all road accidents, including single vehicle accidents. It's illegal to leave the scene of a traffic accident. If you have an accident, don't take photos of the othe
laws.heading: Driving laws

laws.rule: The Islamic holy month of Ramadan is observed in the UAE. Respect religious and cultural customs and laws at this time. Avoid eating, drinking or smoking in public or in front of people who are fasting. Seek local advice to avoid offence. Explore our Ramadan page to learn more, including dates for Ramadan.
laws.heading: Ramadan

laws.rule: The UAE is a mostly Muslim country with conservative standards of dress and behaviour. Take care not to offend. Get familiar with local customs, culture and attitudes before leaving Australia. Research dress codes for tourist attractions, shopping malls, beaches and other public places. These are often displayed onsite or available on websites. Dress modestly, especially in Sharjah and Ajman where Islamic law is enforced. Consider clothing that covers your shoulders and knees. Get local advice if in doubt about appropriate dress.
laws.heading: Dress and behaviour

laws.rule: You can only bring a 3-month supply of medication, whether entering or transiting the UAE. Authorities have detained or deported travellers for: carrying medication to treat HIV/AIDS or hepatitis testing positive for HIV/AIDS or hepatitis Before you leave Australia: check if your medication is legal in the UAE by visiting the Issue of Permit to Import Medicines for Personal Use - Emirates Drug Establishment - EDE Portal and scroll down to ‘Resources’ for semi-controlled medicine list some medications require a permit, you can apply for a permit through the Emirates Drug Establishment website page Issue of Permit to Import Medicines for Personal Use - Emirates Drug Establishment - EDE Portal
laws.heading: Medications

laws.rule: If you're on a tourist visa and want to drive, you must get an International Driving Permit before leaving Australia.
laws.heading: Driving permit

laws.rule: Recreational drones of 5 kg or less must be registered before flying and fly only in the approved zones shown in the My Drone Hub app, in daytime and good weather. GCAA's recreational regulation (CAR-UAR, issue 04) says the pilot must be at least 18 and a UAE resident. Registration is handled through Drones.gov.ae.
laws.heading: Recreational drone rules

closures: official: UAE public holidays are set by Cabinet Resolution No. 27 of 2024 (https://uaelegislation.gov.ae/en/legislations/2595; summary at https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/public-holidays-and-religious-affairs/public-holidays). Fixed-date days for 2027, computed from it: Fri 1 Jan New Year; Thu 2 Dec and Fri 3 Dec National Day. Islamic holidays (Eid Al Fitr 1 to 3 Shawwal, Arafah Day 9 Dhu Al Hijjah, Eid Al Adha 10 to 12 Dhu Al Hijjah, Hijri New Year, Prophet's birthday) are set by moon sighting; no 2027 Gregorian dates have been announced in the pages read, so none are given. The Cabinet may move some holidays to the start or end of the week.

visa-preparation.entry_summary: No visa needed before travel: Australian ordinary passport holders get a tourist visa on arrival. Diplomatic and official passport holders need a visa first, and emergency passports aren't accepted.
visa-preparation.fastest_entry: Tourist visa on arrival at the UAE border, for an Australian ordinary passport.
visa-preparation.before_departure: Check the passport is valid for at least 6 months from the date of entry, has a numerical date of birth (no 'XX') and names in both the first and last name fields. Nothing to lodge online before arrival.
visa-preparation.useful_stay: Not stated on the pages read on 2026-11-03; the stamp given on arrival sets the stay.

steps.step: Travel on an ordinary Australian passport; the tourist visa is given on arrival.
Make sure the passport is valid for at least 6 months from the date of entry.
Passports with 'XX' in the date of birth, or with only one name, are refused entry or transit.
Unresolved charges or unpaid debts in the UAE can lead to detention on arrival, even in transit; check legal status online or with a UAE mission first.
Diplomatic and official passport holders need a visa before travelling; emergency passports aren't accepted.

documents: Ordinary Australian passport valid at least 6 months from entry, numerical date of birth, first and last names

baseline_unverified.host_unlock: A licensed UAE establishment applies for the Mission Work Permit and supplies the official job offer. A regulated profession, including formal teaching, can need the relevant professional licence as well.
baseline_unverified.before_departure: Carry a passport valid for at least six months, onward and accommodation evidence, and a written invitation that separates attendance, meetings, delivery, sales and media activity. Have the host choose any work, event, education or media route before travel.
baseline_unverified.useful_stay: The visitor visa is 30 days. A Mission Work Permit is issued for three months and can be renewed once for a similar period; longer remote or founder plans belong under a residence route.
baseline_unverified.from: Luke's earlier precursor notes; not verified against an official source and not an authority. Kept because no official page covers this point yet.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Ramadan: The Islamic holy month of Ramadan is observed in the UAE. Respect religious and cultural customs and laws at this time. Avoid eating, drinking or smoking in public or in front of people who are fasting. Seek local advice to avoid offence. Explore our Ramadan page to learn more, including dates for Ramadan. Dress and behaviour: The UAE is a mostly Muslim country with conservative standards of dress and behaviour. Take care not to offend. Get familiar with local customs, culture and attitudes before leaving Australia. Research dress codes for tourist attractions, shopping malls, beaches and other public places. These are often displayed onsite or available on websites. Dress modestly, especially in Sharjah and Ajman where Islamic law is enforced. Consider clothing that covers your shoulders and knees. Get local advice if in doubt about appropriate dress. UAE Government: dress modestly, especially in conservative areas and public places such as malls. Transparent, revealing or offensive-slogan clothing is not allowed. Swimwear only at beaches, pools and water parks. Nudity, including sunbathing, is strictly banned. Head covering is not required except at mosques, where women usually wear a headscarf and abaya (provided).
culture-and-protocol.note: Read from the Australian Government's description of local customs.

drone-pilot-pathway.summary: Drone services now run through Drones.gov.ae (UAE Pass login). Recreational drones of 5 kg or less must be registered and fly in approved zones; the recreational rule requires age 18 and UAE residency. Professional operators need security clearance and a GCAA operator authorisation, plus permission for flights in restricted zones.

items.text: Not yet checked: any public GCAA directory of authorised operators.

For professional use GCAA's steps list security clearance, an operator registration letter on letterhead, subscription to GCAA E-Publications and a fee of AED 1,200 (no AUD rate on file), with about three weeks' processing. The authorisation alone does not permit flying: each flight in a restricted (red) zone needs operational permission.

Not yet checked: how a short-term visitor is treated. CAR-UAR (recreational flights, issue 04) says the pilot must be at least 18 and a UAE resident, so a visitor may not qualify for the recreational route.
